component_records.title: Project management and implementation governance
component_records.description: A dedicated project manager and named technical staff run the implementation from award to go-live under a written personnel management plan, with weekly meetings that track progress, budget and timeline against a published schedule. The plan sets out the audit and reporting requirements the City's annual audit imposes on the software, and the team recommends an account structure (fund, department, object, project segments) that supports auditable reporting and is signed off before configuration begins. The team works with the City's Accounting and IT staff on a joint cutover plan with parallel-run and reconciliation checkpoints to reduce downtime and operational impact during the transition. Weekly minutes, a RAID log and a budget-to-actual tracker are issued to the City's project lead after each meeting.

component_records.title: Hosted accounting and financial reporting platform
component_records.description: The bidder hosts and operates a cloud fund-accounting and financial reporting system for the City, licensed for five named users, with no City-side server or database to maintain. The platform captures financial transactions systematically across general ledger, accounts receivable, payroll, utility billing and business licensing, and carries budgeting and forecasting tools that let staff build the annual budget and multi-year projections from the same ledger. Accounts payable includes 1099 preparation and filing, purchasing requisitions, and purchase orders routed through configurable approval hierarchies. Report writing and analysis tools produce the City's financial statements, budget-to-actual reports and ad hoc analysis for Council and management decision-making, and the system retains transaction detail, approval trails and report versions as auditable records. Account number structure is user-defined in format, segment count and length, and the bidder documents that customisation in the response and in Attachment F.

component_records.title: Data migration and financial report writing
component_records.description: The bidder extracts the prior five years of accounting history from the City's current system, maps it to the new account structure, loads and reconciles it, and signs off opening balances with Accounting before go-live. The migration covers general ledger detail, vendor and customer master files, open payables and receivables, payroll history and utility billing balances, with a trial load in a test environment and a documented reconciliation of each fund. The bidder's report writer works alongside City staff to build the financial statements, budget reports and utility billing reports the City needs, and hands over the report definitions with written documentation so staff can maintain them.

component_records.title: Training, manuals and post-implementation support
component_records.description: The bidder delivers personalised training and written manuals for the City's power users in each module, plus at least one recorded training session and a manual available to all staff, delivered virtually and on site at go-live. Support runs for the first 12 months after go-live under a named account manager, with a ticketing help desk that logs, prioritises and reports on every request. The vendor pushes automated software updates and issues change communications describing each release before it lands, and the support team handles annual e-filing of 1099s and W-2s each January. Support continues through annual contract renewals under the same service terms.

component_records.title: Implementation schedule to July 1, 2026 go-live
component_records.description: The bidder commits to a phased schedule that starts at contract award and completes implementation by July 1, 2026, aligned to the start of the City's fiscal year, with configuration, migration, parallel test and cutover milestones dated backwards from that date. The schedule names the City's decision points and staff time required at each stage so the City can plan around its small establishment, and it includes a contingency window before go-live for parallel-run reconciliation.

component_records.title: Price proposal and cost transparency
component_records.description: The bidder submits a price proposal stating a total price for all services and deliverables, a capped total reimbursable expenses figure, and a total price proposal figure that is the sum of the two, with no uncapped reimbursables. The price is the total cost to the City including all materials, supplies and travel, broken out into implementation fee, recurring fees, license fees and support costs, with support costs during implementation separated from post-implementation support. The proposal also estimates the cost of any additional applications or third-party vendors the bidder proposes, and references the specific tasks and deliverables in the scope of work so each line can be traced. The bidder bears all costs of preparing and submitting the proposal and of attending interviews.

component_records.title: Contract, compliance and bid timetable obligations
component_records.description: A contract and compliance workstream owns the non-technical obligations. The bidder reviews the City's standard contract for services before responding and raises any exception as a written question by July 31, 2025, submitting no additional or modified terms with the proposal and accepting that all RFP terms are binding contract conditions and that submission constitutes agreement to Section 4.0 and all other specifications. The bidder files its written questions through the City's stated question channel by the July 31, 2025 deadline, and holds September 25, 2025 for a virtual finalists' interview with the proposed project manager and account manager if the City requires one. The bidder observes the no-contact rule from submission to award, accepting disqualification for any violation the City does not deem harmless, and does not alter its price proposal during any clarification. It provides proof of workers compensation and commercial general liability insurance, signs the Certification of Financial Condition, and notifies the City within 15 days of any material change to those representations. It discloses in Attachment C whether any work is performed outside the United States and gives written notice to the City if personnel are relocated outside the United States during the contract.

component_records.title: Implementation experience and references
component_records.description: The bidder evidences at least three comparable implementations of accounting and financial software for local governments, councils of government or federal grant-funded organisations, with client name, scope, performance dates and contact details for each. Case studies describe the procedural streamlining advice given to each client and the measured efficiency results, and the bidder shows a continuing support record for improvements and daily operations after go-live. The same evidence supports the qualifications and references section of the proposal.

The bidder could also fail to return a complete spreadsheet and be judged nonresponsive. The document is missing from the RFP and the solution's own assumption says its contents are unknown, so a mismatch is expected unless the City supplies it before the deadline.

items.text: Standard City contract unavailable before the question deadline. The City's standard contract for services and the General Contract Terms and Conditions are only available on request and are not in the RFP, yet the bidder must review them, may not attach exceptions, and is deemed to accept all RFP terms by submitting. If the contract carries indemnity, insurance or liability terms the bidder cannot accept, the only chance to raise them is the July 31, 2025 question deadline, which may pass before the document arrives. The contract is missing from the RFP and the RFP bars modified terms with the proposal, so an unacceptable clause found after July 31, 2025 leaves the bidder bound or forced to withdraw.
items.reason: Contract available on request, review required, no modified terms, acceptance on submission, July 31 question deadline all stated in sources.

items.text: Go-live date of July 1, 2026 is a goal, not a fixed start. The City wants go-live on July 1, 2026 to match its fiscal year, but the project starts only soon after award and negotiation, with award listed as October 22, 2025 and no fixed start date. The proposed solution treats July 1, 2026 as a firm contractual date and assumes mobilisation in November 2025; if award slips or negotiations run, the eight-month window for design, migration of five years of history, report writing and parallel test compresses and the date is missed. The RFP states the date as a goal and leaves the start open, while the solution prices a fixed date from an assumed November 2025 start, so the risk turns on facts the RFP does not settle.
items.reason: Goal, award date, and start 'soon after award' supported; the solution's November 2025 mobilisation and firm-date assumption are not in the cited sources.

items.text: Hard copy and emailed proposal both due at the same deadline. The RFP requires a signed original hard copy and an emailed digital copy, and the solution's compliance workstream treats the submission as a single deadline. The RFP does not state a separate hard-copy receipt date or whether receipt is measured by postmark, so a courier delay on August 28, 2025 could make an otherwise responsive proposal late. A late hard copy loses the whole bid, and the RFP leaves the receipt rule unsettled, so the risk turns on a fact the RFP does not give.
items.reason: Hard copy and email requirements, same deadline, late-rejection and no separate receipt rule are in sources; the solution's assumptions are not graded.

items.text: Five years of history migration sized without knowing volumes or formats. The solution commits to migrating five years of general ledger detail, master files, open balances, payroll history and utility billing balances, and assumes the City supplies CSV or Excel extracts from Tyler Technologies. The RFP states no data volumes, source formats or extract responsibilities, so the migration effort, reconciliation work and report writing may be materially larger than priced, and opening balances may not be signed off before go-live. The RFP leaves volumes and formats open and the solution's assumption about CSV extracts is unverified, so extra effort is expected rather than unusual.
items.reason: Five-year import and report writing are supported; the Tyler CSV extracts and the listed data types are not in the cited sources.

items.text: Functional scope of six modules assumed, not confirmed. The RFP lists the modules the City runs today but does not say whether the replacement must cover all of them. The solution assumes all six, including payroll and utility billing, are in scope and licensed for five users; if the City intends fewer modules or more users, the price and the configuration effort are wrong in either direction, and if it intends more users the licence cost rises. The RFP leaves module scope and user count open, and the solution's assumptions are inferences from the current system rather than stated requirements.
items.reason: Modules, five users and current-system listing are in sources; solution assumptions and risk judgment need no support.</br>

items.text: Reimbursable expenses capped with no ceiling or eligible categories given. The City requires a capped reimbursable expenses figure and a total price proposal but sets no cap amount, no eligible expense categories and no rule on whether the total price proposal is the sum of services and the cap. The solution assumes a fixed ceiling covering travel and third-party costs only; if the City expects a different basis, the price is either uncompetitive or under-recovers travel and third-party costs. The RFP leaves the cap basis and the relationship between the three price figures open, so the outcome depends on the City's answer rather than on the bidder's effort.
items.reason: Cap requirement, three price figures and absence of cap amount or categories match sources; solution assumption is judgment.</br>

items.text: Attachment E insurance proof required with no coverage limits stated. The RFP requires proof of workers compensation and commercial general liability insurance as Attachment E but states no limits, additional-insured wording or certificate holder. The solution assumes limits customary for municipal software services; if the City requires higher limits or specific endorsements, the bidder must buy cover it has not priced, and an unacceptable certificate could make the proposal nonresponsive. Insurance is a pass/fail submission item and the limits are unstated, so the cost and the compliance outcome depend on the City's answer.
items.reason: Workers comp and CGL proof as Attachment E, no limits stated; rest is judgment.</br>

items.text: Attachment G security documentation standard undefined. The RFP requires documentation of the measures protecting financial data and the secure access controls implemented, as Attachment G, but sets no format, depth or standard. The solution's hosted platform carries the City's general ledger, payroll and utility billing data, so an incomplete security narrative risks losing points on the 45% scope criterion and, if the City applies a pass/fail reading, the whole proposal. The requirement is mandatory and the evidence standard is unstated, so the bidder cannot tell how much documentation is enough.
items.reason: Attachment G requirement and no format stated are supported; 45% scope criterion and pass/fail reading not in cited sources.</br>

items.text: Offshoring disclosure weighed as added risk and cost. Attachment C requires the bidder to state whether any work is performed outside the United States and to list locations, and the City says it will weigh that as additional risk and cost before award. The solution's compliance workstream handles the disclosure but does not say whether any delivery, support or development is offshore; if it is, the disclosure may cost evaluation points, and if personnel relocate mid-contract the bidder must give notice on a timetable the RFP does not set. The City states the disclosure affects award, and the solution leaves the offshore footprint unstated, so the scoring impact depends on facts not settled in the proposal.
items.reason: Disclosure, locations, City risk/cost assessment, and relocation notice without timetable all match sources.</br>

items.text: Three comparable references with valid emails are a rejection trigger. The RFP requires at least three references for similar local-government implementations with client name, scope, dates, contact name, phone and valid email, and says an invalid email may cause rejection. The solution commits to three comparable implementations but the RFP does not define similar services or recent experience, so references that the City considers out of scope or unreachable could cost the 10% qualifications score or the whole bid. The requirement is mandatory with a stated rejection consequence, and the qualifying standard for similar and recent is undefined.
items.reason: Reference requirements and rejection are supported; 'local-government implementations' wording and 10% qualifications score not in cited sources.</br>

items.text: Certification notice period conflicts between 15 and 30 days. R106 requires notice to the City within 30 days of a material change to the certification, while R148 requires notice to the Contract Lead within 15 days. The solution commits to the shorter 15-day notice to the Contract Lead, which assumes that recipient satisfies both obligations; if the City reads them as two separate duties to two recipients, the bidder could breach the contract on a technicality. The conflict is real but the shorter period is the safer commitment, so the exposure is a compliance argument rather than a delivery failure.
items.reason: 30-day and 15-day notices are supported; R106 says notice to City, not specifying recipient conflict; solution commitment not in sources.</br>
